issues.legal_issue: A municipality cannot withdraw from a statutory setback acquisition once the conditions for vesting are satisfied.
material_facts: The municipality issued a notice under a road-widening scheme requiring a setback from private land.
While compensation proceedings were pending, the municipality sought to withdraw its claim over part of the affected land.
The Court held that the governing Act provided no power to withdraw and that the land vested in the municipality once the statutory conditions were satisfied.
issues.conclusion: The municipality was not entitled to withdraw from the acquisition proceedings; the land vested in it once the requisite conditions were satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 305 of the Madhya Bharat Municipal Corporation Act, 1956, land added to a public street by setting back or removing a building is to be treated as part of the street and vests in the Corporation. The Act provides no power for the Corporation to withdraw from the acquisition proceedings once the statutory conditions are satisfied.

predicates.municipal_setback_acquisition: A municipality undertook a statutory building setback acquisition to widen or improve a public street.
predicates.vesting_conditions_satisfied: The circumstances required for the affected land to vest in the municipality had occurred.

issues.definition: When a municipality undertakes a statutory street-setback acquisition and the vesting conditions have occurred, it cannot withdraw from the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: Solatium is payable in addition to compensation when a District Court determines compensation for compulsorily acquired land under the statutory reference procedure.
material_facts: The landowner applied to the District Court to determine compensation for land affected by the municipal setback scheme.
The District Court awarded compensation and an additional 15 percent solatium.
The Supreme Court approved the reasoning that the Land Acquisition Act provisions governing the basis for determining compensation apply to the District Court proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The District Court was right to award 15 percent solatium in addition to compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 387(3) of the Madhya Bharat Municipal Corporation Act, 1956 directs the District Court, when determining a claim for compensation for land, to follow as far as may be the procedure under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The Court applied section 23(2) of that Act as part of the code governing the basis for compensation, approving and applying The Borough Municipality of Ahmedabad v. Javendra Vajubhai Divatia, I.L.R. [1937] Bom. 632.

predicates.district_court_land_compensation_referen: A District Court determined a compensation claim for land under a statutory reference procedure.
predicates.compulsory_land_acquisition: The land was taken through a compulsory acquisition process.

issues.definition: When a District Court determines a land compensation claim arising from compulsory acquisition under the statutory reference procedure, solatium is payable in addition to compensation.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising statutory revision cannot re-determine the factual sufficiency of compensation fixed by a District Court.
material_facts: The municipality challenged the amount of compensation fixed by the District Court in a revision before the High Court.
The District Court had heard the parties and received evidence before fixing compensation.
The High Court declined to reassess the amount, and the Supreme Court held that it could not determine factual questions about compensation in revision.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to decline to consider whether the compensation was sufficient, because its revisional jurisdiction did not extend to determining questions of fact.
issues.legal_principle: Section 392 of the Madhya Bharat Municipal Corporation Act, 1956 makes District Court decisions subject to High Court revision unless the Act provides otherwise. Even assuming that this revisional power is wider than the power under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, it does not extend to deciding questions of fact or fixing the amount of compensation.

predicates.high_court_revision_from_compensation_or: A party brought a revision before a High Court challenging a District Court order fixing compensation.
predicates.challenge_requires_factual_reassessment: Deciding whether the compensation is sufficient would require the court to reassess factual matters.

issues.definition: When a compensation order is challenged in High Court revision and resolving the challenge requires factual reassessment, the High Court cannot redetermine the compensation amount.
